About your forecast

Harbour is a New Zealand boating and fishing forecast baseline. Weather values are model forecasts.

Weather and marine data: Open-Meteo. Harbour Blend combines ECMWF IFS, NOAA GFS and DWD ICON by default, with confidence based on model agreement. Individual models and automatic best match remain available. Wave models are selected separately. All are delivered through Open-Meteo; this is one API provider, not independent delivery services. Marine data includes Copernicus Marine Service information. Data licences · Marine methodology.

Marine values use the nearest available sea model cell.

Wave height means significant wave height. Individual waves can be larger. Model currents are coarse offshore estimates, not tidal stream predictions for channels or bars.

All forecast times use New Zealand local time. Data is fetched when you open a spot or refresh. After six hours, saved forecasts are marked stale. Offline forecasts always show when they were downloaded.

Tides use published LINZ port predictions for 2026–2027 (CC BY 4.0). Heights are above the port chart datum; weather can change actual water levels. These downloads are not official tide tables for statutory navigation. Marine warnings remain linked to MetService.

Forecasts, preferences and marks stay on this device. Forecast/search coordinates go to Open-Meteo. Chart imagery comes from LINZ via a public ArcGIS archive; coast tiles come from OpenStreetMap and OpenSeaMap. The chart relay requests LINZ tiles using a server-held key. Marks remain on this device.

The map includes LINZ NZ 53 (Hauraki Gulf) depth soundings, contours and symbols under CC BY 4.0. Its source was updated 13 January 2022 and exported 18 April 2023. This is a dated reference chart, not a current navigational ENC. Wider chart coverage uses the separate LINZ chart relay. The same map code runs in the Android app.

How Harbour Blend works

ECMWF IFS, NOAA GFS and DWD ICON supply weather; ECMWF WAM, NOAA GFS Wave and Météo-France supply waves. Each starts with equal weight. Distant outliers have less influence, while the full range remains visible. Directions use a circular mean; weather codes are voted, with storm signals retained.

Confidence is a heuristic index based on model spread, available members and lead time. It is not a calibrated accuracy probability; models can share errors. Supplementary fields do not count as extra model votes. Trip windows use the highest predicted wind, gusts and waves, and exclude low confidence hours.
